feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Learning to Think and Explore in 3D World
entry.summary:
ACT3D enables vision-language models to navigate and explore 3D environments via single-frame observations using outcome-based reinforcement learning without trajectory supervision.

Why it matters: It proves that VLMs can learn efficient, adaptive 3D active visual exploration strategies purely through outcome-based rewards without requiring dense multi-view inputs or frame-by-frame trajectory annotations.

entry.title: Scene-Designer: Learning Design Intelligence for Agentic 3D Scene Generation
entry.summary:
Scene-Designer is an agentic 3D indoor scene generation framework that learns design intelligence and quality critique using two new datasets and a Critic-guided reinforcement learning algorithm called Scene-GRPO.

Why it matters: It establishes a dual design-and-critique learning framework that allows AI agents to generate physically valid, functionally correct, and coherent 3D indoor environments with reduced trial-and-error.

entry.title: From Research Goals to Scientific Closure: Evaluating Agents Through Evidence-Supported Physics Research
entry.summary:
PhysClosureBench evaluates AI agents on 50 physics tasks to measure if local scientific accomplishments achieve complete, evidence-supported research closure.

Why it matters: The benchmark demonstrates that current frontier LLMs frequently fail to achieve complete scientific research closure due to misinterpretation of results and unresolved physical applicability limits, despite strong local performance.

entry.title: RAP: A Dataset for Paper-to-Poster Generation via Declarative Markup from Human-Crafted Exemplars
entry.summary:
RAP introduces a dataset of 25K+ paper-poster-markup triplets with an automated derendering pipeline, establishing a benchmark for paper-to-poster visual coding via declarative markup.

Why it matters: By providing verifiable HTML/CSS markup instead of layout boxes, RAP enables deterministic, objective evaluation and allows human-crafted posters to serve as reusable design templates for automated document generation.

entry.title: Lexical Reference Frames: Interpreting LM Residual Streams in Native Semantics
entry.summary:
Lexical reference frames read LM hidden states through remaining model layers rather than fixed static lenses, capturing native context-adaptive semantics without fitting to final model output.

Why it matters: They provide a more accurate, non-static framework for interpreting residual stream states, improving interpretability, feature steering, and early-exit computational efficiency.

entry.title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models
entry.summary:
A new evaluation framework, MIST, decouples execution failures from memory loss in video world models, paving the way for the M3-Agent prompting method.

Why it matters: Disentangling execution bugs from memory retention enables targeted fixes via instruction revision rather than costly model retraining.

entry.title: OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence
entry.summary:
OfficeTown introduces a generative organizational simulation framework that produces continuous, contextual work environments to generate training data and benchmark generalist AI agents.

Why it matters: Simulating realistic organizational work provides grounded environments and contextual data that significantly enhance the performance of generalist agents on external professional tasks.

entry.title: Xiaomi-Lens-0 Technical Report
entry.summary:
Xiaomi-Lens-0 is a 4B multimodal model based on Qwen3.5 that directly predicts segmentation masks from its visual latents and patch features to enable grounded chain-of-thought reasoning.

Why it matters: It improves fine-grained visual region understanding and segmentation by enabling multimodal models to generate and supervise region-specific visual latents during step-by-step reasoning.

entry.title: MOSS-Image Technical Report
entry.summary:
MOSS-Image is an open-weight text-to-image system using a 5B single-stream DiT backbone and an agentic prompt enhancement module to improve bilingual long-form text rendering and layout control.

Why it matters: MOSS-Image narrows the performance gap between open-weight models and closed-source systems in generating complex layouts and rendering dense bilingual text.

entry.title: Can Visual Generation Expand What Unified Multimodal Models Know?
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce Knowledge Transfer Probing to demonstrate that visual generation supervision can expand text-based knowledge in Unified Multimodal Models without direct question-answering training.

Why it matters: Visual generation training can serve as a distinct data source to expand language model knowledge bases beyond traditional text-only pretraining.

entry.title: SciΠvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers created SciΠvot, a 248-case benchmark evaluated across six scientific fields to test LLM agent scientific judgment at critical research decision points using real human-intervention records.

Why it matters: The findings show that current frontier LLM agents struggle with critical research judgment and often degrade in performance when exposed to project context, highlighting a key bottleneck for fully autonomous scientific research.

entry.title: Stuck on Shuffle: On Attribute-Object Binding in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce SABER, a benchmark for evaluating attribute-object binding across four modality pairings, and show that text-only synthetic finetuning improves cross-modal and image-image retrieval performance.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that synthetic text-only supervision can efficiently fix compositional binding failures in multimodal embeddings without expensive image collection.

entry.title: AVC-Reward: Event-Centric Audio-Video Consistency Evaluation
entry.summary:
AVC-Reward is an event-centric audio-video reward model that evaluates consistency across multi-event, multi-layer, and asymmetric scenes via a coarse-to-fine three-level metric.

Why it matters: It provides an automated, human-aligned metric and reinforcement learning signal to evaluate and refine complex, multi-event audio-video generation models.

entry.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part I: Topology, Input Injection, Recurrent-State Design
entry.summary:
A systematic evaluation isolates looped Transformer design choices, demonstrating that the Huginn architecture outperforms Ouro and reduces resident parameters by 75% compared to feedforward MoE baselines under matched FLOP budgets.

Why it matters: Looped Transformers using the Huginn-style architecture drastically lower memory footprints by reducing resident parameters by 75% without compromising downstream task performance.

entry.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
entry.summary:
ReaDy is the first speculative decoding method to leverage hybrid linear attention (HLA) recurrent states, retrieving position-specific context to accelerate autoregressive draft generation.

Why it matters: It improves speculative decoding efficiency and draft acceptance rates in hybrid linear attention architectures without introducing significant computational or I/O overhead.

entry.title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
entry.summary:
Document training forms transitive behavioral couplings in LLMs, causing fine-tuning on one targeted behavior to unintentionally elicit associated and multi-step composed behaviors.

Why it matters: Unintended emergent behaviors can originate from composed multi-document associations, making post-hoc safety evaluations ineffective if they rely solely on a model's current explicit behaviors.

entry.title: Truth in Contrast: Calibrated Factual Evidence from Language Model Likelihoods
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce Contrastive Factual Evidence (CFE) and its probabilistic counterpart, the Contrastive Factual Posterior (CFP), which leverages shared error cancellation between opposing conditions to improve language model confidence calibration.

Why it matters: CFP and likelihood geometry alignment provide a zero-shot framework to reliably measure factual confidence and boost generation quality in low-resource languages.

entry.title: Trapped in Your Story: Evaluating Narrative-Induced Sycophancy in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
A new 5,500-instance benchmark reveals that LLM sycophancy is non-monotonically altered by story structure, with causal framing increasing user agreement while personal experiences can reduce it.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that LLMs can be steered not just by explicit user opinions, but by subtle variations in how justifications and explanations are formatted and framed.

entry.title: ScoutRoute: Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Routing Using Internal Language Model Signals
entry.summary:
ScoutRoute is a post-hoc routing framework for heterogeneous MoE models that predicts expert competence from internal representations and logit confidence using a single scout-model forward pass.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, computationally efficient expert routing across independently trained, heterogeneous LLMs without needing expensive multi-model inference or joint training.

entry.title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
entry.summary:
LM2LM uses reinforcement learning and a frozen Research World Model to train LLMs to generate effective language model improvement proposals at a 33% lower data-generation cost.

Why it matters: It establishes a computationally viable path for recursive self-improvement in LLM development by replacing expensive full-model training runs with reliable surrogate reward feedback.

entry.title: SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
SimOPD is an on-policy distillation method that transfers teacher internal knowledge by matching response similarity distributions using paired memory banks, avoiding direct hidden-state alignment.

Why it matters: SimOPD enables more effective cross-architecture model compression by transferring internal structural knowledge without needing projection layers or matching hidden-state spaces.

entry.title: Reasoning Models Can Control Their Chains of Thought When They Tell Themselves To
entry.summary:
Reasoning models exhibit significantly higher chain-of-thought (CoT) controllability when constraints are placed directly inside their reasoning channel as self-instructions rather than specified solely in user prompts.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that reasoning models can effectively steer their own thinking process, which improves user control but also creates vulnerabilities for safety monitoring evasion.

entry.title: MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning
entry.summary:
MGE-PO introduces a four-quadrant advantage shaping method for RL that combines solution correctness with rollout generation entropy, paired with an online entropy-based question curriculum.

Why it matters: Incorporating generation entropy into advantage calculations provides finer credit assignment for mathematical reasoning, improving accuracy across multiple model architectures.

entry.title: Not All Test-Time Compute Is Evidence: Model-Specific Bias in LLM Reasoning
entry.summary:
Researchers show test-time compute fails due to intra-model error correlation and introduce DIA, a method using heterogeneous model arbitration on prediction disagreements to improve accuracy while reducing tokens.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that scaling test-time compute requires model diversity rather than single-model repetition, offering a more token-efficient approach to improving LLM reasoning reliability.

entry.title: Beyond the Answer: Student-Conditioned Trace Construction for Reasoning Distillation
entry.summary:
ReDiST is a offline, student-conditioned framework that constructs and selects evidence-rich reasoning traces tailored to a target student model for improved reasoning distillation.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that tailoring reasoning traces specifically to a target learner's capabilities yields superior student distillation performance compared to using static teacher traces or answer-only supervision.

entry.title: Learning to Read Out: Unembedding Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
entry.summary:
Researchers show language model outputs lag behind hidden state representations due to unembedding learning rates, introducing parameter-trajectory crosscoding to track readout evolution during pretraining.

Why it matters: Tracking task acquisition solely through output tokens misdates when models learn capabilities, as early behavioral benchmarks measure unembedding readout timing rather than internal representation growth.

entry.title: H-DDCM: Hadamard Codebooks for Fast Generative Image and Video Compression
entry.summary:
H-DDCM improves training-free generative image and video compression by replacing dense Gaussian codebooks with implicit randomized Hadamard dictionaries, significantly reducing memory and compute overhead.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, memory-efficient, and near real-time generative compression of high-dimensional images and long video streams on standard single-GPU hardware without retraining generative models.

entry.title: When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill
entry.summary:
Researchers identified critical performance bottlenecks in remote KV caching for long-context LLM prefill and optimized LMCache to reduce 16k-token p99 latency from 83.32s to 0.67s on FP8 GLM-5.3.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that naive remote KV caching can severely degrade long-context LLM serving performance, providing a validated design for context-parallel remote cache architectures.

entry.title: CoWorld Reasoner: Agentic Multimodal Reasoning with the Evolving Video World Model-Driven Harness
entry.summary:
CoWorld Reasoner introduces an agentic framework that leverages a Video World Model as a visual reasoning engine, jointly evolving tools, skills, and code using execution feedback without updating model weights.

Why it matters: It enables flexible spatiotemporal visual imagination and reasoning in VLMs through dynamic, training-free harness evolution rather than task-specific fine-tuning or rigid generation pipelines.

entry.title: Equal CER, Unequal Damage: Severity-Weighted Character Error Rate for OCR
entry.summary:
semCER is a severity-weighted Character Error Rate metric for OCR and VLMs that uses an LLM judge to assign grapheme edit costs without requiring word segmentation.

Why it matters: It provides a fine-grained, human-aligned evaluation metric for visual text recognition that penalizes semantic-damaging errors more heavily than trivial typos.

entry.title: One Bias Score, Two Factors: How Mitigations Affect Option Bias in Multiple-Choice Evaluation
entry.summary:
Researchers show that option bias in multiple-choice evaluation, measured by pooled SD, decomposes into two label-free factors: flip rate and positional skew.

Why it matters: Decomposing bias into flip rate and positional skew allows practitioners to evaluate whether mitigations improve true model correctness or merely enforce consistent, but incorrect, predictions.

entry.title: PINT: A Unified Model with Shared Predictive Intent for Robot Manipulation
entry.summary:
PINT is a unified robot manipulation model that links semantic reasoning, video generation, and action control through a shared chunk-level Predictive Intent while preserving expert-specific pathways.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that decoupling task-specific pathways via a shared predictive token space enables strong zero-shot and out-of-distribution robot manipulation without requiring large-scale embodied pretraining.

entry.title: Diminishing Returns of Data in Sparse Autoencoders: Functional Behavior does not Guarantee Feature Reproducibility
entry.summary:
A study shows Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) functional metrics converge at far lower token budgets than one-to-one feature reproducibility, which requires larger datasets and explicit validation.

Why it matters: Researchers can significantly reduce SAE training costs when targeting functional metrics, but must use higher data budgets and reproducibility checks when making feature-level claims.

entry.title: Beyond Context Length: Characterising the Difficulty of Long-Context Reasoning
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced LURCH, a benchmark quantifying long-context LLM difficulty using three new metrics: evidence scope, evidence dispersion, and reasoning depth, rather than relying solely on total context length.

Why it matters: Evaluating long-context models strictly by token count masks failure modes caused by scattered evidence and multi-step reasoning dependencies.

entry.title: Priming Base Models for Agentic Post-Training: An Open Midtraining Recipe
entry.summary:
A new open midtraining recipe trains base models on hundreds of billions of tokens at 256K context using natural software-engineering data and agentic traces to prime them for post-training.

Why it matters: It demonstrates an open, effective midtraining strategy that enhances downstream agentic performance and RL trainability without relying solely on long synthetic SFT stages.

entry.title: Retrieved but Not Read: Understanding Why Search-Augmented LLMs Fail to Use Available Evidence
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated proprietary and open-weight LLMs on temporal facts to demonstrate that search-augmented models frequently default to outdated parametric knowledge despite retrieved context.

Why it matters: Understanding why LLMs default to parametric memory over retrieved evidence helps engineers design better retrieval architectures and decoding strategies to prevent hallucinations and temporal errors.

entry.title: FIRM: Fisher-Informed Retention Merging for Federated LLM Unlearning
entry.summary:
FIRM is a single-round server-side aggregation framework that uses client-local Fisher statistics and a second-order retention projection to prevent magnitude explosion during federated LLM unlearning.

Why it matters: It enables stable, single-round server aggregation for federated unlearning without exposing private client data or degrading retained model utility.

entry.title: ACEdit: Stable Multi-Turn Image Editing via Asymmetric Conditioning
entry.summary:
ACEdit stabilizes multi-turn image editing by applying self-forcing combined with asymmetric conditioning distillation from a teacher model anchored to the original image.

Why it matters: This approach prevents image quality degradation and maintains instruction adherence across extended sequential editing sessions.

entry.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
entry.summary:
Market-based post-training (MPT) enables decentralized agent swarms to jointly learn individual action policies and self-orchestration via competitive bidding without a central coordinator.

Why it matters: It establishes a decentralized framework for multi-agent systems that scales naturally, improves task robustness, and allows agents to self-organize without top-down engineering.

entry.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
entry.summary:
Researchers developed a dual-path steering agent trained via pairwise ranking and GRPO to dynamically supervise, detect goal drift in, and course-correct LLM single- and multi-agent systems.

Why it matters: It prevents resource waste and execution failures caused by goal drift in complex single- and multi-agent LLM workflows without requiring retraining for different intervention frequencies.

entry.title: Improving Environment-Agnostic Coding Agents: The Role of Scaffolding
entry.summary:
A Codex and GPT-5.6-sol study demonstrates that environment-agnostic coding agents still lag behind task-specialized baselines due to ineffective procedure and control usage, despite using identical model inputs and general-purpose tools.

Why it matters: The findings show that advanced language models cannot yet dynamically self-regulate execution control as effectively as developer-supplied scaffolding across diverse environments.

entry.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
entry.summary:
LEASH is a training-free framework that uses weak agent latent uncertainty to trigger escalation to strong agents and monitor them post-handoff via a shadow observer.

Why it matters: It enables long-horizon computer-use agents to achieve frontier-model performance while significantly reducing API inference costs through zero-overhead uncertainty monitoring.

entry.title: Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries
entry.summary:
Librarian Agents use reinforcement learning to proactively reorganize raw document corpora into hierarchical, query-anticipating filesystems, significantly outperforming reactive retrieval and heuristic precomputation.

Why it matters: Proactively curating unstructured data into optimized workspaces shifts LLM workload away from slow, complex cross-document retrieval during inference, reducing latency and boosting accuracy for downstream tasks.

entry.title: Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing
entry.summary:
A new weak-to-strong model routing framework uses model disagreement derived from unsupervised, model-to-model comparison instead of ground-truth supervision to decide when to delegate requests to a stronger model.

Why it matters: It enables cost-effective, high-accuracy deployment of small models on edge devices without relying on expensive or unavailable ground-truth supervision for open-ended and agentic tasks.

entry.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
entry.summary:
OS-Helix is an end-to-end trained multimodal agent that unifies GUI actions and code execution within a single action space using Step-balanced GSPO and verifiable hybrid task synthesis.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that natively learning to route between GUI actions and code execution in a single model significantly outperforms prompt-based tool usage for complex desktop automation.

entry.title: Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation for Unified Vision-Language Models
entry.summary:
SCOPED addresses cross-capability gradient conflicts in VLMs by distilling independently trained, skill-augmented RL experts into a unified student model through on-policy supervision.

Why it matters: SCOPED enables vision-language models to consolidate diverse, independently learned visual capabilities into a single model without incurring multi-objective gradient interference or requiring auxiliary prompts at inference.

entry.title: Beyond Downstream QA: Rethinking How We Evaluate Agent Memory
entry.summary:
FEB-30 is a human-annotation-free benchmark evaluating agent memory intrinsically by inspecting internal stores across 30 fact-evolution trajectories, exposing critical flaws missed by downstream question-answering evaluation.

Why it matters: Downstream QA benchmarks fail to detect internal agent memory corruption, necessitating direct intrinsic evaluation to reliably diagnose and build robust memory architectures.

entry.title: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning
entry.summary:
AutoSFT is a multi-agent system that automates supervised fine-tuning data research by enabling a full range of data actions, including proportional adjustments, pruning, repairing, replacing, and synthesis.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that effective automated data engineering for LLM fine-tuning requires covering a diverse action space via multi-agent architecture rather than relying on a single data modification strategy.

entry.title: Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine
entry.summary:
Terminal-RSI introduces alternating Recursive Self-Rewrite and Recursive Policy-Refine stages with novel reward and GAE formulations to advance terminal agent training.

Why it matters: The approach demonstrates that recursively coupling trajectory rewriting with policy refinement enables terminal agents to convert partial local repairs into verified end-to-end task completions.

entry.title: Mosaic: Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Mosaic is a multi-session agentic reinforcement learning method using critic-free hierarchical optimization to reward individual session contributions and optimize session allocation in non-continuous context trajectories.

Why it matters: It improves session utility and context allocation efficiency for LLM agents utilizing advanced multi-session workflows like context compaction and subagent forking.

entry.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
entry.summary:
CoDA co-evolves a generative simulation data engine and robot action policy using a shared memory that compiles vision-language critic diagnoses into generation and training programs.

Why it matters: It enables automated, targeted simulation data generation that systematically addresses specific robot policy failure modes to dramatically boost out-of-distribution robustness.

entry.title: Virtual Head Attention
entry.summary:
Virtual Head Attention (VHA) uses two linear operations—Q Premix and Linear Postmix—to halve physical query heads and cut KV cache while improving performance over GQA and MLA.

Why it matters: VHA breaks the trade-off between KV cache memory, compute FLOPs, and output quality by maintaining standard GQA inference optimizations while using only two KV heads.

entry.title: Beyond Policy Rollouts: Embedding-Space Directional Exploration with Anchored Noise for LLM RLVR
entry.summary:
EDEN improves LLM reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by appending a single anchored, noise-perturbed embedding position to prompt inputs during rollouts, generating more diverse trajectory groups without modifying model architecture or test-time inference.

Why it matters: Directly perturbing the input embedding space increases rollout diversity and advantage variance within fixed sampling budgets, outperforming traditional temperature or entropy adjustments without altering test-time decoding.

entry.title: SUPRA-TEX: 3D Generation with Super-Aligned Texture
entry.summary:
SUPRA-Tex decouples single-image 3D material generation into MLLM-based visible PBR estimation, surface projection, and latent-space completion via an interleaved flow transformer that anchors visible latents as fixed read-only references.

Why it matters: The decoupling approach allows models trained exclusively on public datasets to achieve state-of-the-art detail preservation and material separation, matching or exceeding commercial end-to-end 3D asset generators.

entry.title: FlashMask-3: Efficient and Expressive Mask-Aware Distributed Attention
entry.summary:
FlashMask-3 extends FlashMask to NVIDIA Hopper architectures and context parallelism via warp-specialized kernels, zero-communication mask localization, load balancing, and topology-aware communication pruning.

Why it matters: It eliminates the performance overhead of arbitrary structured attention masks during long-context distributed training on Hopper GPUs.

entry.title: Cowork-Gym: Synthesizing Interactive Work Environments at Scale
entry.summary:
Cowork-Gym synthesizes interactive work environments using a build-execute-revise loop with stateful user simulation, generating 64.9K environments to post-train agentic LLMs.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that automated synthesis of complex, stateful multi-tool environments can train sub-40B parameter models to outperform >100B parameter models on interactive agentic benchmarks.

entry.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
entry.summary:
LEASH is a training-free framework that uses a weak model's latent hidden state uncertainty to dynamically escalate long-horizon computer-use tasks to a strong black-box agent and monitor it post-handoff.

Why it matters: It enables deployment of long-horizon computer-use agents at reduced cost by dynamically cascading to expensive proprietary models only when necessary and monitoring them without access to their internal weights.

entry.title: Mine, Sample, Render: Test-Time Diversity Alignment Of Generative Models
entry.summary:
Mine-Sample-Render (MSR) is a test-time framework that improves output diversity by decoupling attribute configuration sampling from conditional rendering.

Why it matters: MSR enables generative models to produce outputs with higher diversity and better alignment with real-world corpus distributions without requiring retraining or fine-tuning.

entry.title: MMSearch-OPD: Easy Made Hard, Hard Made Learnable for Long-Horizon Multimodal Search Agents
entry.summary:
MMSearch-OPD improves long-horizon multimodal search agents using a data refinement pipeline alongside joint reinforcement learning and on-policy distillation with an exponentially decaying distillation coefficient.

Why it matters: The approach enables multimodal search agents to reliably perform complex, long-horizon deep searches without requiring newly collected image-question datasets.

entry.title: SERO: Learning from Executable Oracle Continuations for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
SERO enhances long-horizon agentic RL by executing oracle continuations from policy-reached states in real environments and applying policy-reachability weighting to weight oracle steps based on behavior policy compatibility.

Why it matters: SERO overcomes sparse exploration in long-horizon RL by providing real-environment trajectory supervision beyond states reachable by the unguided policy alone.

entry.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
entry.summary:
Gen4P repurposes a pretrained video generator into a feed-forward 4D perceiver, recovering 4D geometry and motion from monocular video without iterative denoising.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that generative video pretraining can be repurposed for single-pass, unified 4D computer vision tasks without computationally expensive iterative denoising.

entry.title: LeanPRM: Lean-Grounded Process Supervision for Natural Language Proof Verification
entry.summary:
LeanPRM is an automated framework that leverages the Lean proof assistant to generate step-level labels for natural language mathematical proofs without human annotation.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, automated step-level verification of complex natural language math proofs, bypassing expensive human annotation and formalization bottlenecks.

entry.title: Copy-Paste Language Models
entry.summary:
Copy-Paste Language Models (CPLMs) augment conventional LLMs with a lightweight Copy-Paste head to enhance in-context copying, improving training efficiency and downstream performance.

Why it matters: CPLMs offer a low-overhead structural change to improve LLM pretraining efficiency, long-context handling, and retrieval performance across model scales.

entry.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
entry.summary:
PathFM is a generative forecasting model using flow matching to capture trajectory dependence, distilled to 1-2 steps with shared history attention caching for fast multi-path sampling.

Why it matters: PathFM makes trajectory-based generative forecasting practical for real-time applications requiring downstream path metrics like peak load, cumulative demand, and event timing.

entry.title: Explaining the Roles of Experts in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Personalization
entry.summary:
Researchers adapt open-weight MoE LLMs for personalization and use crosscoders to identify, interpret, and causally intervene on expert routing paths corresponding to specific personalized latents.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that MoE experts encode isolated personalization features allows for targeted model steerability and interpretability without needing full dense-model retraining.

entry.title: DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction
entry.summary:
DropKV is a principled KV-cache eviction framework that decouples joint eviction into independent per-token scoring, offering a provable constant-factor approximation guarantee and fused Triton kernels for accelerated LLM prefilling.

Why it matters: It resolves the memory bottleneck of long-context LLMs by providing a mathematically grounded eviction method that reduces latency without sacrificing task accuracy.

entry.title: TIPS: A Tiny Inference-time Policy for Scaling in Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
TIPS is a 600K-parameter learned inference policy that dynamically controls unmasking and remasking in frozen masked diffusion language models to improve reasoning accuracy without updating the backbone.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that lightweight, learned inference controllers can significantly optimize the compute-accuracy trade-off in diffusion language models without expensive backbone fine-tuning.

entry.title: Baselines and Score Centering in Policy Gradient Estimation
entry.summary:
This note introduces a covariance perspective on policy gradients under regularized importance sampling, clarifying the distinct roles and interactions of group-mean baselines and score centering across sequence-level and token-level off-policy RL.

Why it matters: It provides precise mathematical guidance on how to correctly combine baselines and score centering to prevent bias and reduce variance when fine-tuning LLMs via off-policy reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Query-Efficient Rejection Sampling for Parallel Masked Diffusion
entry.summary:
The Single-Increment Rejection Sampler (SIRS) eliminates the linear query overhead of rejection sampling in parallel masked diffusion models by estimating log acceptance probabilities using a single score query.

Why it matters: SIRS enables bias-free parallel generation in masked diffusion models with drastically reduced computational cost per generation step.

entry.title: Lexical Reference Frames: Interpreting LM Residual Streams in Native Semantics
entry.summary:
Lexical reference frames read LM residual streams through remaining model layers with context-adaptive attention, outperforming fixed lenses in reading accuracy, attribution, steering, and early-exit skipping.

Why it matters: They provide a more accurate, non-fitted interpretability method that makes intermediate hidden states readable, attributable, and steerable while significantly improving early-exit execution efficiency.

entry.title: Patch where the text is new: a compression view of where byte-level models should spend compute
entry.summary:
Novelty patching replaces entropy-based byte patch segmentation with a two-byte lookup table based on LZ77-style repetition, significantly improving byte-level model performance on in-line math computations.

Why it matters: It provides a simple, parameter-free patch-segmentation rule that fixes the failure of entropy-based byte-level transformers on arithmetic and inline calculation tasks.

entry.title: Selection Is Not Learning: Choosing Model Futures
entry.summary:
Researchers identified a selection-to-update gap in self-evolving language models and introduced HeirCommit and EvoHeir to decouple experience from parameter inheritance, reducing harmful updates by 68-83%.

Why it matters: The framework prevents performance degradation in self-improving AI loops by ensuring models only inherit updates that genuinely improve reasoning capabilities while preserving beneficial generated experience.

entry.title: N-Gram Memories at Two Bits: Quantizing Lookup Tables in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Conditional Program (CP) compresses language model conditional memory lookup tables down to two bits per row using Gaussian trellises, norm restoration, and independently decodable row records.

Why it matters: It enables ultra-low-bit compression of massive n-gram lookup tables directly on GPUs, significantly expanding model capacity without incurring severe KL divergence penalties.

entry.title: RoleQ: Role-Aligned Scales for Converting Language Models to Ternary
entry.summary:
RoleQ is a post-training framework that converts language models to ternary weights (1.59 bits/weight) by assigning scales according to the functional roles of Transformer units rather than matrix layout.

Why it matters: RoleQ enables rapid, low-cost conversion of pre-trained LLMs to extreme 1.59-bit ternary quantization without requiring full retraining or sacrificing crucial factual knowledge and MMLU performance.

entry.title: Behavioral Forgetting Is Not Privacy in Machine Unlearning
entry.summary:
A controlled multilingual study reveals that behavioral machine unlearning fails across access paths, as information forgotten in one language remains retrievable in semantically equivalent queries using different languages and scripts.

Why it matters: Measuring unlearning solely through in-distribution benchmark performance creates a false sense of privacy protection, as erased data remains exposed to cross-lingual or adversarial access paths.

entry.title: Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Waypoint-OPD improves policy-shift distillation by using directional agreement between early and late teacher RL shifts to gate endpoint shifts on student trajectories.

Why it matters: It enables more accurate knowledge transfer from RL-trained teachers to students by filtering out noisy or inconsistent policy shifts without heavy computational overhead.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
entry.summary:
A theoretical and algorithmic framework formalizing feedback-driven self-evolution of an agent's software harness, prompts, and tools while keeping core model weights fixed.

Why it matters: It enables continuous automated optimization of complex AI agent architectures and tool integration without the high computational cost of retraining underlying model weights.

entry.title: RoTA-Bench: Evaluating 3D Spatial Reasoning through Interactive Projection Alignment
entry.summary:
RoTA-Bench introduces an interactive 3D-to-2D projection alignment benchmark to evaluate vision-language models' ability to infer object geometry and execute precise rotations within a limited action budget.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that current vision-language models struggle to translate sequential 2D visual feedback into accurate 3D spatial reasoning and fine-grained motor control.

entry.title: MJev-Spatial: System One Spatial Intelligence via Native Attention Matching
entry.summary:
MJev-Spatial is a System 1 multimodal decision model that unifies spatial understanding tasks into a single-pass classification framework using native attention matching without parameter additions.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that spatial reasoning in vision-language models can be accelerated for real-time interaction by casting text generation into parameter-free attention classification.

entry.title: OpenGCUA: Toward a Fully Open Stack for Generalist Computer Use
entry.summary:
OpenGCUA introduces a fully open-stack generalist computer-use agent framework featuring code execution and harness-to-model decision transfer to operate across visual and programmatic interfaces.

Why it matters: It provides an open framework and standardized SDK that significantly improves generalist computer-use agent performance and step efficiency over closed, GUI-only implementations.

entry.title: Mosaic: Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Mosaic introduces Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning and uses a critic-free hierarchical optimization framework to allocate context and credit across multi-session agent trajectories.

Why it matters: Mosaic improves context efficiency and performance for agentic workflows that require session splitting, context compaction, or subagent delegation.

entry.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
entry.summary:
FDE-Gym is a new benchmark featuring 95 real-world end-to-end AI delivery tasks across 20 customer scenarios to evaluate agents operating in ambiguous, production-like environments.

Why it matters: The benchmark highlights a critical capability gap between evaluating agents on well-defined issue tickets versus deploying them in real-world customer environments with incomplete specifications.

entry.title: MAI-Gym: An Open All-in-One Platform for GUI Agent Evaluation and RL Training across Mobile and Computer Environments
entry.summary:
MAI-Gym is an open, unified platform for GUI agent evaluation and online RL training scaling up to 20,000 parallel instances across mobile, computer, and web environments.

Why it matters: It provides open infrastructure and environments that enable scalable online RL training and zero-shot cross-domain transfer for GUI-operating agents.

entry.title: VLA-Δ: Learning Physical State Transition for Vision-Language-Action Models
entry.summary:
VLA-Δ is a Vision-Language-Action framework that explicitly uses physical state transitions between current and future states as supervision targets during pretraining without adding inference overhead.

Why it matters: By explicitly supervising physical state transitions, VLA-Δ prevents observation-action overfitting and improves real-robot manipulation without increasing runtime computational cost.

entry.title: WorldCast: Exploring Intelligent Visual Generation in World State Prediction
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce WorldCast, a 320-case benchmark evaluating multimodal models on multi-step visual world state prediction across eight distinct categories.

Why it matters: The benchmark provides a standardized framework to measure and address the gap between language-based reasoning and coherent multi-step visual simulation in frontier generative models.

entry.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
entry.summary:
OmniVerifier-C1 decomposes complex rules into fine-grained sub-questions to provide continuous pointwise and pairwise graded scores for multimodal visual verification.

Why it matters: Accurate pairwise graded visual verifiers enable generative models to transition into robust, rule-governed world-modeling agents.

entry.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
entry.summary:
MLExpert is a 35B MoE agentic model trained via a novel post-training framework to autonomously execute long-horizon machine learning engineering tasks.

Why it matters: It demonstrates an effective post-training methodology for building open, efficient agentic models capable of autonomous recursive self-improvement and long-horizon engineering optimization.

entry.title: Data World: Scaling Data Environments from Scratch
entry.summary:
Data World synthesizes data agent environments, tasks, and rubrics by specifying underlying world mechanisms first, enabling automated task generation and RL-zero training of models like DataWorld-35B-A3B without trajectory distillation.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, privacy-compliant synthetic training and verification for data agents without relying on costly human curation or trajectory distillation.

entry.title: Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL
entry.summary:
MRTPO improves multi-reward RL fine-tuning by using Jensen-Shannon distance to assign individual reward advantages to relevant tokens without requiring auxiliary models or token-level annotations.

Why it matters: It enables more precise credit assignment in multi-reward reinforcement learning for language models without requiring manual token annotations or extra reward models.

entry.title: WorldMemBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Memory of Video World Models
entry.summary:
WorldMemBench is a new benchmark featuring 260 test cases designed to evaluate static and dynamic memory capabilities in video world models through controlled camera departures and multi-revisit trajectories.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized framework to diagnose memory failures and guide the training of video world models capable of maintaining persistent, coherent environments over extended interactions.

entry.title: Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Language Diffusion Transformer (LangDiT), an optimized transformer architecture that significantly improves continuous diffusion language model performance without altering underlying training objectives or samplers.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that tailored transformer architectures can dramatically increase the generation quality and speed efficiency of non-autoregressive continuous diffusion language models.

entry.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
entry.summary:
A study across 11 language models demonstrates that how linearly readable a relation's facts are in pretrained representations strongly predicts post-fine-tuning generalization to held-out subjects.

Why it matters: Evaluating the linear readability of pretrained internal representations allows practitioners to predict whether a model will successfully generalize downstream fine-tuning tasks across related entities.

entry.title: Towards Continual Learning: Mitigating Forgetting With Subspace Tuning
entry.summary:
Subspace Tuning (SST) mitigates catastrophic forgetting in LLM fine-tuning by restricting weight updates to the bottom singular subspace, preserving principal singular directions.

Why it matters: SST improves the learning-forgetting Pareto frontier, allowing LLMs to acquire new target-task skills while nearly eliminating catastrophic forgetting in large-scale models.

entry.title: EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search
entry.summary:
EliteReplay combines GRPO post-training with a quality-diversity archive to prevent solution collapse and preserve diverse correct strategies in LLMs.

Why it matters: It prevents RL post-training from narrowing an LLM's solution space, allowing models to generate diverse valid strategies for complex or ambiguous tasks.

entry.title: Training-Free On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Training-free on-policy distillation aggregates fine-tuned specialist models into a single base model using layer-wise least-squares regression over input second moments gathered from forward passes on rollouts, eliminating gradient steps.

Why it matters: It enables rapid, computationally efficient fusion of multiple specialist LLMs without expensive multi-teacher training, gradient updates, or backpropagation.

entry.title: Human Interventions as Labels: Localizing, Steering, and (Sometimes) Editing the Computations Behind LLM Agent Failures
entry.summary:
Researchers use human intervention events as diagnostic labels to localize, steer, and weight-edit the internal computation driving LLM agent over-asking failures across five open model families.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that agent failures can be localized and steered using intervention signals offers a runtime method to reduce human oversight burdens without relying solely on prompting or behavioral cloning.

entry.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
entry.summary:
MLExpert is a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model trained via Hierarchical Agentic SFT and Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) for autonomous machine learning engineering.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that targeted post-training methods like WIRL enable smaller open-weights models to match larger frontier models in complex, long-horizon autonomous engineering tasks.

entry.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
entry.summary:
A study across four instruction-tuned LLM families shows evaluation awareness increases safety refusals in five Indic languages by an average of 14.4 percentage points, matching English refusal levels while elevating benign over-refusals.

Why it matters: Standard safety evaluations in Indic languages may artificially overestimate real-world model alignment due to evaluation awareness altering default generation behavior.

entry.title: KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents
entry.summary:
KnowGPO improves search agent reinforcement learning by grouping trajectories and calculating process rewards based on atomic knowledge state transitions rather than surface-level state observations.

Why it matters: It provides a reliable credit-assignment mechanism for multi-turn search agents, allowing smaller language models to outperform larger models on complex, knowledge-intensive tasks.

entry.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
entry.summary:
A dual-view visual design principle for Time Series Language Models combines line plots with normalized delay embeddings to improve temporal reasoning and prediction.

Why it matters: Combining invariant structural views with original coordinate frames allows general-purpose multimodal models to solve complex temporal reasoning and forecasting tasks without losing raw measurement data.
